# FDG4024

> DO provide at least one API that consumes each interface you define (a method taking the interface as a parameter or a property typed as the interface).

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 4.6 Interface Design.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Not an analyzer candidate: the consuming API can ship in another assembly of the framework, which one compilation cannot see.

## From the book

Doing this helps to validate the interface design. For example, `List<T>.Sort` consumes the `IComparer<T>` interface.
